reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: reducing interstitial impurities (O, N) in Ti-Ni alloys is well-known to prevent embrittlement and phase instability, and extending this to a single-phase HEA to maintain solid-solution strengthening at high temperature is a logical, well-supported mechanism.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and decisive: fabricating two sets of samples with controlled impurity levels and comparing their high-temperature mechanical properties and microstructural segregation directly addresses the hypothesis, with a well-defined falsification criterion.
reasons.usefulness: This is a highly useful hypothesis for the field, as it addresses a critical practical issue (impurity control) in Ti-Ni HEAs for high-temperature applications and proposes a straightforward, impactful intervention that researchers would want to test.
